inputs.note: Frozen fixture: its text is part of the judge cache key, so editing it is a visible change to a committed file. Measured both ways over five rounds: stable under the committed prompt (5/5, 15/15), but a generic rubric splits 3-2 across rounds, so this one does not reliably detect a loosened prompt. It is here as an alive-check on a project-specific failure mode. W2-M6 and W2-M8 are the factually_consistent drift detectors.

expected: The judge grades a value the source did not print, reached by converting the value it did print, as a fail.
guards_against: A judge that has stopped working, on the mg/dL vs mmol/L misread this suite exists to catch — a value that is arithmetically right and is not what the page says. It does NOT guard against a loosened prompt: a generic rubric grades it fail on two rounds in five. W2-M6 and W2-M8 are the fixtures that do.
